title: Solo Testers Scored 99% Right, Yet 75% Lied When 5 Strangers Disagreed
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Solomon Asch (1951-1956): Perceptual Line-Judgment Conformity & One-Ally Liberation, grounded in Solomon E. Asch (1956) (Psychological Monographs: General and Applied). Empirical findings show that starting in 1951 at Swarthmore College and published in full monograph form in 1956, Solomon Asch tested 123 male college students seated among 7 to 9 secretly briefed confederates.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: On each of 18 trials, the experimenter held up two large white poster cards: one standard vertical black line on the left and three comparison lines labeled 1, 2, and 3 on the right.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Solomon E. Asch (1956). Studies of independence and conformity: I. A minority of one against a unanimous majority. Psychological Monographs: General and Applied. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0093718
- Frank Mertesdorf, Helmut E. Lueck, Ernst Timaeus (1969). Heartrate in an Asch-Type Conformity Situation. Perceptual and Motor Skills. https://doi.org/10.2466/pms.1969.29.2.565
- Alen Hajnal, Jennifer Vonk, Virgil Zeigler-Hill (2020). Peer influence on conformity and confidence in a perceptual judgment task. Psihologija. https://doi.org/10.2298/psi190107018h

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
